name: velaris
description: Write Velaris, see what it can touch, and run it in a box.
long_description:
Velaris is a language where a function's signature declares its types, the effects it may perform, whether it can fail, and promises a theorem prover checks before the program runs.

This connector gives four tools: read the language card (about 3,700 words, enough to write correct Velaris), check a program without running it, audit what it can touch and how much of its promises are proven, and run it under an effect budget you choose. A program run with allow: ["io"] cannot read files, reach the network or call Python, whatever its source claims - and a refusal cannot be caught by the program.

The server grants at most io unless it is started with --max-allow: a run that asks for files, the network, the environment, the clock, randomness or Python is refused, and the refusal names what the server grants. This bundle starts the server without --max-allow, so it grants io only. It also holds each run to 30 seconds and 512 MB unless started with --max-timeout and --max-memory-mb: a run may ask for less, and asking for more is refused.

Not a security boundary: a server started with --max-allow ffi grants everything Python can do.

tools.name: velaris_card
tools.description: The Velaris language, small enough to read before writing it.

tools.name: velaris_check
tools.description: Compile without running; problems with codes, lines and fixes.

tools.name: velaris_audit
tools.description: What a program touches, promises, and can fail at.

tools.name: velaris_run
tools.description: Run under an effect budget; anything outside it is refused. Grants at most io unless the server is started with --max-allow.
